renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: sequence_count
  title: Sequences kept
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of sequences in the filtered FASTA, with the number of distinct samples beside it. It answers how many sequences the annotation steps receive.
    How to read: compare it with the count before filtering to see how many sequences were removed. A count of zero means the filter removed everything.
    Source: https://bioinf.shenwei.me/seqkit/
  column: sample
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: sequences, and the samples they come from
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: sequence_length
  title: Sequence length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median length of the kept sequences, in residues for a protein FASTA and in bases otherwise, with the shortest and longest beside it. The histogram shows how the lengths are spread. It answers whether the kept sequences are of the expected size.
    How to read: a narrow histogram means uniform sequences. A long tail of very short sequences can be fragments, and a very long one an unfiltered chimera, so check the table for the outliers.
  column: length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: median, with the distribution

- component: figure
  title: Sequence length distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the sequences in a length bin, coloured by sample. It answers how the lengths are distributed and whether one sample differs from the others.
    How to read: overlapping peaks mean similar samples. A sample that sits apart holds sequences of a different size, so open the table to inspect them.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: length
    color: sample
    labels:
      length: Sequence length
      sample: Sample

- component: table
  title: Sequences
  description: |-
    Each row is a sequence of the filtered FASTA with its id, sample, header description and length. It answers which sequences passed the filter.
    How to read: sort by length to find the shortest and longest sequences, or search the description to find one by name.
  columns:
  - entity
  - sample
  - description
  - length
